findings.problem: Pressing Add a moment on a plan that is already live rewrites the two objects at the top of the page that say who is holding it. Driven from a fresh load of ?state=owner-flight at 1440x960 and 390x844, on paper and on ink, identically: .b-shared goes 'Live since 15 July - anyone with the link can read it' -> 'Only you can see this', and the primary verb goes 'Get the link' (103px) -> 'Publish' (75px). Because the bar group is right-anchored at 1254, the narrower verb drags the other two controls inward: Add a moment 925 -> 953, Preview 1060 -> 1088. So the button the owner just pressed slides 28px out from under the cursor, and the header cluster re-lays out on a click that has nothing to do with it. Pressing Undo removes the moment but does not restore the record: the plan reads 'Only you can see this' for the rest of the session. render-b.js:1249 sets F.publication = { state: 'draft' } unconditionally; its own comment says the write exists for the owner-empty path, where the plan has never been handed to anyone. The behaviour gate proves the verb only on first paint (interaction-check.mjs: 'the publish verb knows whether anyone is holding a copy'), so nothing catches the add path.
findings.fix: At render-b.js:1249, make the downgrade conditional on the plan never having been shared rather than unconditional: replace `F.publication = { state: "draft", publishedAt: null };` with `if (!F.milestones.length) { F.publication = { state: "draft", publishedAt: null }; }` so the first moment on an empty project still starts as a draft while a live plan keeps its record. Leave the F.updatedLabel write and the paintPublication(root) call where they are - the stamp SHOULD move. Write the gate assertion first and watch it fail: open state=owner-flight, click [data-act="add"], assert .b-shared still starts 'Live since' and [data-act="publish"] still reads 'Get the link'.

findings.element: .b-editGroup - span.b-label 'What guests see' and div.b-seg (Shown / Hidden)
findings.problem: The label runs into the control it names. Measured with the editor open, identical on paper and ink and at 390, 768, 1023 and 1440: .b-label ink ends at 154.4 and .b-seg's border box starts at 154.4, with its border ink at 155.4 - a 1.0px gap, and about 2.8px from the last glyph once the 1.76px trailing letter-space is discounted. At 5x the final E of SEE is visibly against the black Shown pill. There is no .b-editGroup rule anywhere in master.html: it is a bare block holding an inline span next to an inline-flex, so the only thing between them is whatever the markup emits, which is nothing. That makes it the one same-line object pair in the file whose spacing is on none of the nine declared steps, in a file whose space ladder is otherwise gated. It is also the only label in the panel that does not sit on its own line - 'What it is' and 'When' both do - so the row breaks the panel's label/field rhythm as well as its spacing.
findings.fix: Add one rule beside the existing .b-editActs declaration (master.html:1221): `.b-editGroup { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--gap-control); flex-wrap: wrap; }` - the same shape .b-editActs already uses, on the same declared token. Verified by injection: the gap becomes exactly 12px at 390 and 1440 on both grounds, the row stays 39px tall, and it wraps cleanly below 320 where the two objects no longer fit side by side. Gate it by asserting .b-seg.getBoundingClientRect().left - .b-label.getBoundingClientRect().right === 12 with the editor open.

findings.problem: The rule that spends the indigo a second time is unscoped, so it paints every rail in the file - including the one that runs backwards. Measured on state=day with Behind you opened, paper and ink, 390 and 1440: the ONLY rail on the page is .b-back .b-rail, and it computes to rgb(79,70,229) at opacity 0.5 for its full 634px. That is the accent the lock defines as 'the part of the rail that is still ahead' running down nine moments that are behind, on the one screen where nothing is ahead any more. The file already knows this: the .b-back comment five lines above the rule says the past is 'quieter than what is ahead, and carrying no accent - nothing behind you is the next thing'. The declaration at line 967 sits later at equal specificity and silently overrides it - the same late-declaration failure class the lessons file records for state rules killing hover. Nobody caught it in nine rounds because accent=structure was not the shipping room until now.
findings.fix: Scope the second spend so it cannot reach the backward measure. After master.html:967 add: `[data-accent="structure"] .b-back .b-rail { background: var(--fore-16); opacity: 1; }`. Verified by injection on both grounds: the days-back rail returns to rgba(17,17,17,0.16) on paper and rgba(255,255,255,0.16) on ink, and the forward rail on owner-flight is untouched at rgb(79,70,229)/0.5. Gate it by asserting on state=day with the disclosure open that .b-back .b-rail's computed background is not the accent.

biggestWin: The rail is a real time axis, not a list with a line beside it. Driven at 1440, the distance from today's mark to the 16-day tick is 404px and from there to the 23-day tick is 178px - 25.25 and 25.4 pixels per day - so the empty stretch between 16 July and 1 August is the fortnight itself, drawn, and 'nothing is planned until 1 August' is something the owner sees before reading. It holds at every width (two pixels a day on the backward measure, declared as data-px), it holds on both grounds with identical geometry, and the tick centres sit on the rail to within 0.0px at all 35 widths I swept including the half-pixel stage offsets. Everything else composes around it correctly: the horizon is sticky in its own track, both desk panes fade only where something is actually cut (data-fold above/below/both, 48px, state-driven), focus scrolls the plan pane rather than the page, and 14 states x 6 viewports x 2 grounds produced zero horizontal overflow. That axis is what a studio would have spent months finding, and it is already found.
